# Usage and reproducibility

<!-- completed-manuscript-rerun-provenance -->
**Archive version:** Of the 1,020 results in `data/table_archive.csv`, the 360 main-table results come from the completed rerun with $R=1000$ and $B=1000$ (source: `rerun_main_20261006`). The other 660 are historical extension results and were not rerun. Default `archived` mode rebuilds saved tables without simulation. Resume an existing run with its frozen Rmd input and dependencies; edited files have different hashes.
<!-- /completed-manuscript-rerun-provenance -->

Knit in **`archived`** mode to validate saved CSV values and rebuild the tables. The main-table archive has been checked against the completed rerun and updated LaTeX. Set `mode` to **`rerun`** to execute the simulations in `R/`.

The historical archive records seed `20260925`, but its original code, random-stream mapping, samples, and replicate p-values were not retained. The new code reproduces the design and test procedure; exact recovery of those historical random experiments is not guaranteed. Seeds are not searched to match archived values.

Keep this Rmd beside `R/` and `data/`. Rendering requires `rmarkdown`, `knitr`, and Pandoc; statistical calculations use base R. New results and checkpoints default to `../simulation_results/`. Generated HTML can be deleted and rebuilt.

```{r usage, eval=FALSE}
# Smoke check only; not for manuscript estimates.
rmarkdown::render(
  "01_reproduce_tables.Rmd",
  params = list(mode = "rerun", profile = "smoke", R = 20, B = 99),
  output_file = "01_reproduce_smoke.html"
)

# Main tables: 180 scenarios, each with k=1 and k=3 (360 results).
rmarkdown::render(
  "01_reproduce_tables.Rmd",
  params = list(mode = "rerun", profile = "manuscript", R = 1000, B = 1000, workers = 1),
  output_file = "01_reproduce_full.html"
)

# Full archive grid, including extensions (1,020 results).
rmarkdown::render(
  "01_reproduce_tables.Rmd",
  params = list(mode = "rerun", profile = "archive", R = 1000, B = 1000, workers = 1),
  output_file = "01_reproduce_archive_grid.html"
)
```

# Simulation design

Each group contains $m$ independent, zero-mean observations in $p$ dimensions with covariance $\Sigma$. Transform $W=\Sigma^{1/2}Z$ using the **symmetric positive-definite square root**.

| Code | Standardized vector $Z$ |
|:---|:---|
| N | Independent standard normal coordinates |
| T | $\sqrt{6/Q}H$, $Q\sim\chi^2_8$, $H\sim N(0,I_p)$; one shared $Q$ per observation |
| E | $\sqrt{E}H$, $E\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)$; one shared mixing variable per observation |
| G | $\sqrt{V}H$, $V\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(3,1/3)$, with scale $1/3$; one shared mixing variable per observation |
| L | Independent standard logistic coordinates scaled by $\sqrt{3}/\pi$ |

| Covariance | Definition |
|:---|:---|
| C1 | $I_p$ |
| C2 | Entry $(i,j)$ is $0.5^{|i-j|}$ |
| C3 | First five diagonal entries are 4; the rest are 1 |
| C4 | First block has size 4; remaining blocks have size 2; each block is $0.4I_d+0.6J_d$ |

The 15 distribution pairs comprise five identical-distribution and ten different-distribution pairs. All satisfy the equal-covariance $H_0$; only identical-distribution pairs are exchangeable controls.

The main tables use $(p,m)=(10,50),(10,150),(40,150)$ and $k=1,3$. Extensions also include $p=20,40$, $m=50,150$, and $k=1,2,\min\{\lfloor\log m\rfloor,\lfloor p/2\rfloor\}$.

Sample covariances use denominator $m-1$ and recomputed group means. The statistic is $\sqrt m$ times the sum of the largest $k$ **absolute eigenvalues** of the covariance difference. Each independent permutation uniformly selects $m$ pooled raw observations for the first group. The upper-tail p-value is

$$\widehat p=\frac{1+\sum_{b=1}^B\mathbf 1\{T_b\geq T_{\rm obs}\}}{B+1},\qquad
\text{reject if }\widehat p\leq\alpha.$$

Within each scenario and replicate, all $k$ share data and permutations. Covariances computed from group sums and second moments are algebraically equivalent to `cov()`. Replicate seeds depend on the master seed, scenario, replicate, and purpose; execution order and worker count do not affect results.

# Validate and rebuild the archive

```{r archived-data}
archived <- read_archived_results()
manuscript_archived <- select_manuscript(archived)
# Check the 360 rerun main-table results by scenario key, not row order.
paper <- read.csv(
  file.path(.slads_source_root, "data", "manuscript_reference.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ii <- match(archive_key(paper), archive_key(archived))
stopifnot(
  nrow(paper) == 360L, !anyNA(ii),
  all(paper$rejection_rate == archived$rejection_rate[ii]),
  all(paper$mcse == archived$mcse[ii])
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Item = c("Archived results", "Main-table results", "Replicates R", "Permutations B"),
  Value = c(nrow(archived), nrow(manuscript_archived), 1000, 1000)
))
```

# Run the selected mode

`rerun` saves configuration, source hashes, replicate p-values and rejection indicators, summary CSVs, and session information, with checkpoints every 10 replicates. Matching inputs, dependencies, and configuration allow resumption. `source_snapshot/` preserves the Rmd, R modules, and archive data used. The run directory depends on their full contents, so even comment edits create a new directory; resume old runs with frozen inputs.

`workers` defaults to 1 and is capped at 7, with one BLAS/OpenMP thread per worker. Windows runs serially. Use the smoke profile to estimate runtime.

```{r run}
if (params$mode == "archived") {
  result <- NULL
  table_data <- if (params$profile == "archive") archived else manuscript_archived
  result_dir <- file.path(params$output_root, "archived")
  dir.create(result_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  write.csv(table_data, file.path(result_dir, "archived_table_values.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  provenance <- "Saved results: 360 main-table rerun values and 660 historical values; no simulation in this Knit"
} else {
  grid <- slads_grid(params$profile)
  result <- slads_run(
    grid, R = params$R, B = params$B, alpha = params$alpha, seed = params$seed,
    workers = params$workers, resume = params$resume, output_root = params$output_root
  )
  table_data <- result$summary
  table_data$k <- as.integer(sub("KyFan_k", "", table_data$method, fixed = TRUE))
  table_data$R <- params$R
  table_data$B <- params$B
  result_dir <- result$directory
  provenance <- "New R simulation; original historical random streams are unavailable"
}
write_paper_tex(table_data, file.path(result_dir, "tables.tex"))
cat("Source: ", provenance, "\nOutput directory: ", result_dir, "\n")
```

# Tables

Entries are rejection rates (Monte Carlo standard errors). Archived results use $R=B=1000$ and $\alpha=0.05$; reruns use the current configuration. Smoke runs show dashes for unrun scenarios without filling them from the archive.

```{r tables, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
groups <- unique(table_data[c("p", "m", "k")])
for (i in seq_len(nrow(groups))) {
  g <- groups[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("\n\n## p=%d, m=%d, k=%d\n\n", g$p, g$m, g$k))
  tab <- format_paper_table(table_data, g$p, g$m, g$k)
  print(knitr::kable(
    tab, align = c("l", rep("c", ncol(tab) - 1L))
  ))
}
```

# Rerun versus archived results

In `rerun` mode, the table below compares new and archived results. Main-table values should agree when seeds, implementation, and design match the completed rerun. The independent-difference MCSE applies only to independent simulations, not as a tolerance for identical random streams. Historical extensions may differ because their original random streams are unavailable.

```{r differences}
if (!is.null(result)) {
  at <- match(archive_key(table_data), archive_key(archived))
  comparison <- table_data[c("p", "m", "covariance", "pair", "k", "rejection_rate", "mcse")]
  comparison$archived_rate <- archived$rejection_rate[at]
  comparison$difference <- comparison$rejection_rate - comparison$archived_rate
  old_exact_se <- sqrt(comparison$archived_rate * (1 - comparison$archived_rate) / 1000)
  comparison$independent_difference_mcse <- sqrt(comparison$mcse^2 + old_exact_se^2)
  write.csv(comparison, file.path(result_dir, "new_vs_archived.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(head(comparison, 30), digits = 4)
}
```
